speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, please describe your symptoms in detail. Specifically, can you tell me exactly where your severe abdominal pain is located, and have you noticed any blood in your urine or changes in urination frequency?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old female. The patient presents with a 5-day history of severe abdominal pain and cramping, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. She reports pain with urination and also experienced burning pain during sexual intercourse 3 days ago. She mentions being sexually active with one male partner, using condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID) secondary to chlamydia or gonorrhea. The combination of severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, dysuria, and post-coital pain in a sexually active adolescent female with inconsistent condom use is highly suggestive of an ascending pelvic infection. I will now request a urine pregnancy test, a urine culture, and a pelvic examination to confirm the diagnosis and rule out other causes.
